questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Antibiotics that are protein synthesis inhibitors:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Amoxicillin is a beta-lactam that inhibits cell wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins (transpeptidases).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ceftriaxone is a third-generation cephalosporin, also a beta-lactam cell wall synthesis inhibitor.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Macrolides bind the 50S ribosomal subunit and block translocation, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Tetracyclines bind the 30S subunit and prevent aminoacyl-tRNA attachment to the A site.

questions.pearl: Protein synthesis inhibitors: 30S = aminoglycosides, tetracyclines; 50S = macrolides, chloramphenicol, clindamycin, linezolid (buy AT 30, CCEL at 50).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Beta blockers block beta-2 bronchodilation and can precipitate severe bronchospasm; asthma is a contraindication.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Topical timolol reduces aqueous humour production by the ciliary body, lowering intraocular pressure in open-angle glaucoma.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Theophylline toxicity causes beta-adrenergic tachyarrhythmias; cautious beta blockade (esmolol, propranolol) is used to control them.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Beta blockers are not a treatment for COPD; non-selective agents may worsen bronchospasm.

questions.pearl: Timolol is the classic topical beta blocker for open-angle glaucoma; it acts by decreasing aqueous secretion.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Theophylline/aminophylline (methylxanthines) are add-on bronchodilators in chronic asthma, limited by a narrow therapeutic index.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Formoterol is a long-acting beta-2 agonist used with inhaled corticosteroids for maintenance (and MART) therapy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Beta blockers cause bronchoconstriction and are contraindicated in asthma.

options.label: D
options.explanation: CCBs have no established role in the treatment of asthma.

questions.pearl: Never give a LABA alone in asthma; always combine with an inhaled corticosteroid.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Amitriptyline is a tertiary amine TCA blocking reuptake of noradrenaline and serotonin; also used for neuropathic pain.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sertraline is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Imipramine is the prototype TCA, also used for nocturnal enuresis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Duloxetine is a serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor (SNRI), not a tricyclic.

questions.pearl: TCA overdose: anticholinergic signs, seizures and wide QRS; treat cardiotoxicity with sodium bicarbonate.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fexofenadine is a second-generation, non-sedating H1 blocker that does not cross the blood-brain barrier.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Diphenhydramine is a first-generation H1 blocker with marked sedative and anticholinergic effects.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chlorpheniramine is a first-generation (classical) H1 antihistamine; mildly sedating.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Levocetirizine, the active enantiomer of cetirizine, is a second-generation antihistamine.

questions.pearl: First-generation antihistamines are lipophilic, cross the BBB and cause sedation; second-generation ones are largely non-sedating.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Itching is the hallmark symptom, from mast cell histamine release in a type I hypersensitivity reaction.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lid oedema and chemosis are common due to increased vascular permeability.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Conjunctivitis does not affect ocular alignment, so diplopia is not a feature.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Mild photophobia occurs, especially in vernal keratoconjunctivitis with corneal involvement.

questions.pearl: Itching = allergic; purulent discharge = bacterial; watery discharge with preauricular node = viral conjunctivitis.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: A congenital laryngeal web narrows the glottis and presents with stridor and a weak cry.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Adenoid hypertrophy causes nasal obstruction, mouth breathing and snoring (stertor), not laryngeal stridor.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A laryngeal or tracheal foreign body causes sudden stridor, especially in toddlers.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A large quinsy with surrounding oedema can extend to the larynx and compromise the airway, producing stridor.

questions.pearl: Commonest cause of stridor in a neonate/infant: laryngomalacia; inspiratory stridor localises to the supraglottis/glottis.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: In myopia parallel rays focus in front of the retina; corrected with a concave (minus) lens.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Presbyopia is an age-related loss of accommodation (anomaly of accommodation), not a true error of refraction.

options.label: C
options.explanation: In hypermetropia rays focus behind the retina; corrected with a convex (plus) lens.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Unequal corneal or lens curvature in different meridia gives astigmatism; corrected with cylindrical lenses.

questions.pearl: Presbyopia usually starts around 40 years and is corrected with convex lenses for near work.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dry beriberi causes symmetrical sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Wet beriberi causes high-output cardiac failure with peripheral oedema.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Dermatitis is a feature of niacin deficiency (pellagra), not thiamine deficiency.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Diarrhoea belongs to pellagra (dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia), not beriberi.

questions.pearl: Thiamine deficiency in alcoholics: Wernicke encephalopathy (confusion, ophthalmoplegia, ataxia); give thiamine before glucose.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.text: Tinea versicolor is a disease of the summer season
options.explanation: Malassezia proliferates in hot, humid conditions, so pityriasis versicolor is commoner in summer.

options.label: B
options.text: Griseofulvin is highly effective for tinea corporis
options.explanation: Griseofulvin is fungistatic against dermatophytes and is effective for tinea corporis and capitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Dermatophytoses spread by direct contact, fomites or animals; they are not classed as sexually transmitted infections.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Topical steroids suppress local immunity and modify lesions (tinea incognito), worsening fungal infection.

questions.pearl: Griseofulvin is ineffective against Malassezia (pityriasis versicolor) and Candida; use azoles instead.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Beta-2 blockade causes bronchoconstriction; asthma is an absolute contraindication.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Beta blockers are first-line for stable angina, reducing heart rate and myocardial oxygen demand.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loss of beta-2 vasodilation may worsen claudication and Raynaud phenomenon (relative contraindication).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Beta blockers (timolol) are used to treat glaucoma.

questions.pearl: Other beta blocker cautions: heart block, decompensated heart failure, Prinzmetal angina, and masking of hypoglycaemia in diabetics.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: TOF has a ventricular septal defect, not an ASD; an added ASD makes it pentalogy of Fallot.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Right ventricular outflow obstruction (usually infundibular stenosis) determines the severity of cyanosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The aorta overrides the VSD and receives blood from both ventricles.

options.label: D
options.explanation: TOF causes right ventricular hypertrophy, giving the boot-shaped heart on chest X-ray.

questions.pearl: TOF: commonest cyanotic congenital heart disease after infancy; hypercyanotic spells relieved by squatting (knee-chest position).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dengue virus (4 serotypes) belongs to the family Flaviviridae, transmitted by Aedes aegypti.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dengue virus is a single-stranded, positive-sense RNA virus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: NSAIDs and aspirin worsen thrombocytopenia-related bleeding and gastritis; paracetamol is used for fever.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Plasma leakage in the critical phase needs careful crystalloid fluid therapy guided by haematocrit.

questions.pearl: Rising haematocrit with a falling platelet count signals plasma leakage in dengue - the critical phase.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: A vaccine is preventive, not a treatment for established infection; management is supportive.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Paracetamol is the analgesic and antipyretic of choice, especially until dengue is excluded.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Aspirin is avoided in the acute phase because of bleeding risk and possible co-existing dengue.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Adequate fluids (oral or IV if dehydrated) are part of supportive care.

questions.pearl: Chikungunya: alphavirus spread by Aedes; hallmark is severe, often persistent polyarthralgia.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: CT findings in stroke (haemorrhagic and ischaemic):

options.label: A
options.explanation: Acute blood is dense and appears white on non-contrast CT.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Infarcted tissue is oedematous and hypodense; early CT may be normal.

options.label: C
options.explanation: An established infarct appears as a hypodense area in a vascular territory.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acute haemorrhage is hyperdense; it becomes hypodense only weeks later.

questions.pearl: Non-contrast CT is the first investigation in acute stroke to exclude haemorrhage before thrombolysis.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Components of the Glasgow Coma Scale:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Verbal response is scored 1-5.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Eye opening is scored 1-4.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Best motor response is scored 1-6 and is the most predictive component.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sensory response is not part of the GCS.

questions.pearl: GCS ranges 3-15; a score of 8 or less usually indicates the need for airway protection (intubate).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Inflammation raises fibrinogen and immunoglobulins, increasing rouleaux formation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: SLE characteristically gives a high ESR, often with a normal CRP unless there is infection or serositis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Increased red cell mass slows sedimentation, so ESR is low in polycythaemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Rising fibrinogen in pregnancy physiologically increases ESR.

questions.pearl: Low ESR: polycythaemia, sickle cell disease, spherocytosis, hypofibrinogenaemia, severe heart failure.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Components and functions of bile salts:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Jaundice results from raised bilirubin; reduced bile salts cause fat malabsorption and steatorrhoea.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Primary bile acids (cholic, chenodeoxycholic) are synthesised from cholesterol in the liver.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Bile salts form micelles that allow absorption of fats and vitamins A, D, E and K.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Water-soluble vitamins do not need micelles for absorption.

questions.pearl: Bile salts are reabsorbed in the terminal ileum; ileal resection causes bile acid diarrhoea and gallstones.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hyperthyroidism, not hypothyroidism, is a classic cause of AF; hypothyroidism causes bradycardia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dilated or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy causes atrial stretch and fibrosis, triggering AF.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Binge drinking causes AF ('holiday heart syndrome').

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pneumonia and acute illness are common precipitants of AF.

questions.pearl: Commonest causes of AF: hypertension, ischaemic heart disease, rheumatic mitral valve disease, thyrotoxicosis, alcohol.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.text: HDL is involved in reverse cholesterol transport
options.explanation: HDL carries cholesterol from peripheral tissues back to the liver.

options.label: B
options.explanation: LDL is taken up via LDL (apo B-100) receptors to supply cholesterol to tissues.

options.label: C
options.text: LDL helps in synthesis of steroid hormones
options.explanation: Adrenals and gonads take up LDL cholesterol as substrate for steroidogenesis.

options.label: D
options.text: Presence of more LDL is good for health
options.explanation: High LDL promotes atherosclerosis; it is the main target of statin therapy.

questions.pearl: HDL is the 'good' cholesterol; LDL is the main atherogenic lipoprotein (familial hypercholesterolaemia = LDL receptor defect).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Secondary syphilis gives a generalised non-itchy maculopapular rash involving palms and soles.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Measles rash is maculopapular, starting behind the ears and spreading downward.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Dengue causes a maculopapular or confluent erythematous rash with 'islands of white'.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Herpes zoster produces a dermatomal vesicular rash.

questions.pearl: Rash on palms and soles: secondary syphilis, hand-foot-mouth disease, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, erythema multiforme.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Banana is rich in carbohydrate (about 90 kcal/100 g) and is a common quick energy food.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Rice is the staple carbohydrate in Bangladesh, providing about 345 kcal per 100 g uncooked.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Apples are mostly water and fibre (about 50 kcal/100 g) and are not regarded as energy-rich.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Water contains no calories and provides no energy.

questions.pearl: Energy yield: carbohydrate 4 kcal/g, protein 4 kcal/g, fat 9 kcal/g, alcohol 7 kcal/g.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: The cornea is avascular; vascularisation causes loss of transparency.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Uniform, regularly spaced stromal collagen lamellae minimise light scattering (Maurice lattice theory).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Corneal nerves lose their myelin sheath after entering the cornea, preserving transparency.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The cornea is non-pigmented; pigment would block light transmission.

questions.pearl: Corneal transparency also depends on relative dehydration maintained by the endothelial Na-K ATPase pump.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Extracellular calcium stabilises membranes; hypocalcaemia causes neuromuscular hyperexcitability and tetany.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Calcium influx at the nerve terminal triggers vesicle exocytosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Calcium is coagulation factor IV, required at several steps of the cascade.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Calcium triggers insulin secretion but is not required for insulin's action on target tissues.

questions.pearl: Chvostek and Trousseau signs indicate latent tetany from hypocalcaemia.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: A stone impacted in Hartmann's pouch with sterile bile gives a mucocele of the gallbladder.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Gangrenous cholecystitis can perforate, causing localised abscess or biliary peritonitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Gallstones are the commonest cause of acute pancreatitis worldwide.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Appendicitis is not a complication of gallstones; gallstone ileus obstructs the terminal ileum.

questions.pearl: Gallstone ileus triad (Rigler): small bowel obstruction, pneumobilia, ectopic gallstone.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Serum albumin below 30 g/L results from heavy urinary protein loss.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Nephrotic syndrome causes hyperlipidaemia as the liver increases lipoprotein synthesis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Proteinuria above 3.5 g/24 h in adults defines nephrotic syndrome.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Low oncotic pressure and sodium retention cause generalised (anasarca) oedema.

questions.pearl: Nephrotic syndrome is hypercoagulable (loss of antithrombin III): watch for renal vein thrombosis.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hypoglycaemia is the commonest acute complication of treatment with insulin or sulfonylureas.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Symmetrical glove-and-stocking sensory neuropathy is the commonest microvascular complication.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Severe hyperglycaemia leads to DKA or hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Diabetes is a major macrovascular risk factor for ischaemic stroke.

questions.pearl: Microvascular complications: retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy; macrovascular: IHD, stroke, peripheral vascular disease.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Clostridia are spore-forming obligate anaerobic Gram-positive bacilli.

options.label: B
options.explanation: B. fragilis is the commonest anaerobe in intra-abdominal infections.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Most streptococci are facultative anaerobes; obligate anaerobic cocci are Peptostreptococcus.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lactobacilli are anaerobic or microaerophilic (aerotolerant) Gram-positive bacilli.

questions.pearl: Metronidazole covers obligate anaerobes; anaerobic infections typically produce foul-smelling pus and gas.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Neisseria are Gram-negative intracellular diplococci.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Corynebacterium is a Gram-positive club-shaped bacillus (Chinese letter arrangement).

options.label: C
options.explanation: E. coli is a Gram-negative bacillus of the Enterobacteriaceae.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Yersinia (e.g. Y. pestis) is a Gram-negative coccobacillus with bipolar staining.

questions.pearl: All cocci are Gram-positive except Neisseria, Moraxella and Veillonella.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Vaccines in the EPI schedule of Bangladesh:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Measles-rubella vaccine is given at 9 and 15 months under EPI Bangladesh.

options.label: B
options.explanation: BCG is given at birth or first contact.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Rabies vaccine is given for post-exposure (or high-risk pre-exposure) prophylaxis, not in routine EPI.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hepatitis B is part of the pentavalent vaccine given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks.

questions.pearl: Pentavalent vaccine = DPT + Hepatitis B + Hib, given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks with OPV and PCV.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Post kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis appears after treatment and acts as a parasite reservoir.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Intercurrent dysentery and diarrhoea are classic complications in immunosuppressed kala-azar patients.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Immune-complex glomerulonephritis and renal amyloidosis can produce nephrotic-range proteinuria.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Secondary bacterial infections such as pneumonia and TB are common causes of death.

questions.pearl: Kala-azar (L. donovani, sandfly): fever, massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia, hyperpigmentation; rK39 test for diagnosis.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Typhoid classically shows relative bradycardia (Faget sign) - pulse slow for the degree of fever.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Rose spots are faint salmon-coloured macules on the trunk in the second week.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pea-soup diarrhoea may occur, though constipation is common early, especially in adults.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Soft, mildly tender splenomegaly appears by the second week.

questions.pearl: Typhoid: blood culture positive in week 1, Widal from week 2, stool/urine culture in week 3; bone marrow culture is most sensitive.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hepcidin-mediated iron sequestration gives normocytic or microcytic anaemia with high ferritin.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lead inhibits ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase, impairing haem synthesis; basophilic stippling is seen.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Defective haem synthesis causes iron-laden ring sideroblasts and microcytosis (in the hereditary form).

options.label: D
options.explanation: B12 deficiency impairs DNA synthesis, giving macrocytic megaloblastic anaemia.

questions.pearl: Microcytic anaemia mnemonic TAILS: Thalassaemia, Anaemia of chronic disease, Iron deficiency, Lead, Sideroblastic.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Typhoid causes mild, soft splenomegaly from reticuloendothelial hyperplasia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chronic malaria is a classic cause of massive splenomegaly (hyper-reactive malarial splenomegaly).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chronic myeloid leukaemia causes massive splenomegaly; acute leukaemias cause moderate enlargement.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pancreatitis does not usually enlarge the spleen, except rarely via splenic vein thrombosis.

questions.pearl: Massive splenomegaly: CML, myelofibrosis, kala-azar, chronic malaria, thalassaemia major.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ruptured ectopic pregnancy causes haemoperitoneum and shock - a life-threatening emergency.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Inevitable or incomplete miscarriage can cause heavy bleeding needing urgent evacuation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hyperemesis is an obstetric condition managed medically, not a gynaecological emergency.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fibroids are usually chronic and managed electively; emergencies (torsion, red degeneration) are uncommon.

questions.pearl: Any woman of reproductive age with abdominal pain and collapse: ruptured ectopic until proven otherwise - check urine hCG.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Asthma is not a leading cause of under-5 deaths.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Diarrhoeal disease is among the top causes of under-5 mortality in low-income countries.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pneumonia is the leading infectious killer of children under 5.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Undernutrition underlies roughly 45% of under-5 deaths.

questions.pearl: Leading causes of under-5 deaths: neonatal conditions (prematurity, birth asphyxia, sepsis), pneumonia, diarrhoea, with malnutrition as an underlying factor.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Clinical features of pneumonia in a child under 2 years:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Stridor in a calm child is a danger sign classifying severe pneumonia or very severe disease in IMCI.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fast breathing, grunting and nasal flaring indicate respiratory distress.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cavitation is not a feature of typical childhood pneumonia; it suggests TB, staphylococcal or Klebsiella infection.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lower chest wall indrawing is an IMCI sign of pneumonia needing treatment.

questions.pearl: IMCI fast breathing: 60 or more/min under 2 months, 50 or more for 2-12 months, 40 or more for 1-5 years.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Migratory polyarthritis of large joints is the commonest major manifestation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Evanescent, non-itchy rash with serpiginous margins on the trunk.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fever is a minor criterion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Raised ESR or CRP is a minor criterion.

questions.pearl: Major Jones criteria (JONES): Joints, carditis (O - heart), Nodules, Erythema marginatum, Sydenham chorea.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Upper GI bleeding usually presents as melaena or haematemesis, not fresh rectal blood.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Left-sided colorectal cancer presents with fresh blood mixed with stool.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Diverticular bleeding is a common cause of painless massive lower GI haemorrhage in the elderly.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Haemorrhoids cause bright red bleeding that drips or streaks after defecation.

questions.pearl: Massive upper GI bleeding with rapid transit can occasionally present as fresh rectal blood (haematochezia).

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: DRE is part of evaluating rectal bleeding to exclude a rectal tumour, followed by proctoscopy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: In acute anorectal abscess DRE is extremely painful; examination is done under anaesthesia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: DRE assesses prostate size and consistency - smooth, firm and enlarged in BPH.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A hard, nodular prostate with obliterated median sulcus suggests carcinoma.

questions.pearl: Internal haemorrhoids are not palpable on DRE unless thrombosed; proctoscopy is needed to see them.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Smoking causes about 90% of lung cancers; risk relates to pack-years.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ionising radiation including radon gas exposure is an established risk factor.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Asbestos increases lung cancer risk and acts synergistically with smoking; it also causes mesothelioma.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Betel quid chewing is linked to oral cavity cancer, not bronchogenic carcinoma.

questions.pearl: Small cell lung cancer is most strongly associated with smoking; adenocarcinoma is the commonest type in non-smokers.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Starvation produces ketoacids, giving a raised anion gap acidosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Loop and thiazide diuretics cause metabolic alkalosis (contraction alkalosis); acetazolamide is the exception.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mineralocorticoid excess in Cushing syndrome causes hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Failure to excrete acid and regenerate bicarbonate causes metabolic acidosis.

questions.pearl: Raised anion gap acidosis (MUDPILES): Methanol, Uraemia, DKA, Paraldehyde, Iron/INH, Lactic acidosis, Ethylene glycol, Salicylates.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Causes of mal-union / impaired union of fracture:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Infection at the fracture site impairs healing and is a major cause of delayed and non-union.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Good blood supply promotes healing; poor vascularity (e.g. scaphoid, femoral neck) impairs union.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Excessive movement from inadequate immobilisation disrupts callus and causes faulty union.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Poor bone quality impairs fixation and healing, contributing to faulty union.

questions.pearl: Mal-union = union in a faulty position; non-union = failure of union, typically from poor blood supply, infection or excessive movement.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Lavage is not contraindicated in arsenic poisoning and may be used early.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Corrosives risk oesophageal or gastric perforation; lavage is absolutely contraindicated.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Lavage is not contraindicated in iron poisoning (activated charcoal does not bind iron).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lavage can provoke vagal stimulation and arrhythmia; unstable dysrhythmias are a contraindication.

questions.pearl: Other lavage contraindications: hydrocarbons (kerosene - aspiration risk), convulsions, unprotected airway in coma.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Marfan syndrome results from autosomal dominant FBN1 (fibrillin-1) mutations.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hereditary spherocytosis is mostly autosomal dominant (ankyrin, spectrin defects).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cystic fibrosis is autosomal recessive (CFTR gene).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Wilson disease is autosomal recessive (ATP7B gene).

questions.pearl: Autosomal dominant diseases are usually structural (Marfan, ADPKD); recessive ones are usually enzymatic.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is water-soluble.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Vitamin D is fat-soluble and stored in adipose tissue.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Vitamin B12 is water-soluble, though stored in the liver for years.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Vitamin K is fat-soluble; malabsorption or obstructive jaundice causes deficiency and raised INR.

questions.pearl: Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K - deficient in steatorrhoea and obstructive jaundice; toxicity possible with excess.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hookworm filariform larvae penetrate the skin of bare feet.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Schistosoma cercariae penetrate skin in fresh water (swimmer's itch).

options.label: C
options.explanation: The New World hookworm also enters through the skin.

options.label: D
options.explanation: E. histolytica is a protozoan acquired by ingesting cysts (faeco-oral).

questions.pearl: Strongyloides also enters through skin and can autoinfect, causing hyperinfection in immunosuppressed patients.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cushing ulcer is a stress ulcer associated with head injury or raised intracranial pressure.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hypovolaemia and myoglobinuria can cause acute kidney injury after major burns.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Curling ulcer is the acute stress ulcer of the duodenum seen in major burns.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Disfigurement and pain commonly cause depression and post-traumatic stress.

questions.pearl: Parkland formula: 4 mL x weight (kg) x %TBSA of Ringer's lactate over 24 h, half in the first 8 hours.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Chlorpheniramine is a first-generation H1 blocker.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fexofenadine is a second-generation non-sedating antihistamine (active metabolite of terfenadine).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Levocetirizine is a second-generation antihistamine.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Promethazine is a highly sedating first-generation phenothiazine antihistamine, also an antiemetic.

questions.pearl: Promethazine is used for motion sickness and as a sedative premedication because of its strong central effects.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Malignancies that commonly show generalised spread:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Disseminated malignancy commonly involves bone, a frequent site of widespread metastasis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lymphoma spreads through lymphatics to multiple node groups and extranodal sites.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Leukaemia is systemic from the outset, involving marrow, blood, spleen and liver.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Primary brain tumours rarely metastasise outside the CNS (no lymphatics, blood-brain barrier).

questions.pearl: Glioblastoma spreads locally and via CSF (drop metastases) but almost never outside the CNS.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: S. aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes are the main causes of cellulitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: S. aureus is the commonest cause of acute endocarditis, especially in IV drug users.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Post-infectious glomerulonephritis classically follows Streptococcus pyogenes infection.

options.label: D
options.explanation: S. aureus is the commonest cause of acute haematogenous osteomyelitis.

questions.pearl: Salmonella osteomyelitis is characteristic of sickle cell disease, though S. aureus remains common overall.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cystic hygroma is a lymphatic malformation typically in the posterior triangle (lateral neck).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sublingual/submental dermoid cysts arise in the midline along lines of embryonic fusion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Branchial cyst lies laterally at the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Tuberculous cold abscess usually arises from lateral cervical lymph nodes.

questions.pearl: Midline neck swellings: thyroglossal cyst (moves on tongue protrusion), dermoid, thyroid isthmus, submental node, plunging ranula.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Achondroplasia (FGFR3 mutation) is the commonest skeletal dysplasia causing disproportionate short stature.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chronic undernutrition causes stunting.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Renal rickets, acidosis and GH resistance cause growth failure.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Klinefelter (47,XXY) patients are tall with eunuchoid proportions.

questions.pearl: Tall stature syndromes: Klinefelter, Marfan, homocystinuria, gigantism; short: Turner, achondroplasia, hypothyroidism, GH deficiency.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Structures that do not have lymphatic supply:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The CNS parenchyma lacks conventional lymphatics (CSF and glymphatic drainage instead).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Middle ear mucosa has lymphatics draining to retropharyngeal and parotid nodes.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Bone marrow has no lymphatic vessels.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The eyeball (except the conjunctiva) lacks lymphatics.

questions.pearl: Other structures without lymphatics: cartilage, cornea, epidermis, internal ear, splenic pulp.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Aspirin does not treat heart failure; it is used only for co-existing coronary disease.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Nitrates reduce preload and relieve pulmonary congestion in acute heart failure.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loop diuretics relieve fluid overload and pulmonary oedema.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Non-dihydropyridine CCBs are negatively inotropic and worsen systolic heart failure.

questions.pearl: Mortality-reducing drugs in HFrEF: ACE inhibitor/ARNI, beta blocker, MRA (spironolactone), SGLT2 inhibitor.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Interrupted sympathetic supply to the dilator pupillae gives miosis with ptosis and anhidrosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Argyll Robertson pupils are small, irregular, accommodate but do not react to light.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cocaine blocks noradrenaline reuptake and causes mydriasis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Demyelinating brainstem lesions can interrupt central sympathetic pathways, producing a Horner-type miosis.

questions.pearl: Pinpoint pupils: opioids, organophosphates, pontine haemorrhage.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Treatment of severe dehydration (WHO Plan C):

options.label: A
options.explanation: Severe dehydration needs rapid IV rehydration; ORS is started only once the child can drink (or by NG tube if IV is unavailable).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Zinc for 10-14 days reduces the duration and severity of diarrhoea.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ringer's lactate 100 mL/kg is given IV, in 1 h + 5 h for infants or 30 min + 2.5 h for older children.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Feeding, including breastfeeding, should continue as soon as possible to prevent malnutrition.

questions.pearl: Plan C: 100 mL/kg Ringer's lactate - infants 30 mL/kg in 1 h then 70 mL/kg in 5 h; older children 30 min and 2.5 h.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Personality change and irritability occur in early encephalopathy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Reversal of the sleep-wake cycle is an early sign.

options.label: C
options.explanation: RUQ pain is not a feature of encephalopathy; it suggests a hepatobiliary cause.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Flapping tremor (asterixis) is a classic sign of metabolic encephalopathy.

questions.pearl: Precipitants of hepatic encephalopathy: GI bleeding, infection, constipation, hypokalaemia, sedatives, diuretics; treat with lactulose and rifaximin.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Atony is the commonest cause of PPH (about 80%).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Genital tract trauma (vaginal, perineal tears, rupture) is a key cause.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Choriocarcinoma may cause late irregular bleeding but is not a cause of PPH in the usual sense.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cervical lacerations cause bleeding despite a well-contracted uterus.

questions.pearl: Causes of PPH - the 4 Ts: Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bleeding time reflects platelet number and function; it is prolonged in thrombocytopenia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Haemophilia A (factor VIII deficiency) prolongs APTT, with normal bleeding time.

options.label: C
options.explanation: vWF is needed for platelet adhesion, so bleeding time is prolonged (APTT may be too).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Factor IX deficiency affects the intrinsic pathway (APTT), not bleeding time.

questions.pearl: Platelet-type bleeding: mucosal bleeding and petechiae; coagulation-type bleeding: haemarthrosis and deep muscle bleeds.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: GH is a 191-amino-acid polypeptide from the anterior pituitary somatotrophs.

options.label: B
options.explanation: GH promotes growth, protein synthesis and cell proliferation via IGF-1.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Somatotropin is the alternative name for GH.

options.label: D
options.explanation: GH rises with stress, exercise, hypoglycaemia and sleep, acting as a counter-regulatory hormone.

questions.pearl: GH excess: gigantism before epiphyseal closure, acromegaly after; diagnose with failure of GH suppression on OGTT.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bacterial meningitis shows neutrophil predominance; lymphocytes suggest viral or tuberculous meningitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bacteria and neutrophils consume glucose, giving a low CSF/blood glucose ratio.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Increased BBB permeability raises CSF protein.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Raised ADA is a marker of tuberculous meningitis.

questions.pearl: Pyogenic CSF: turbid, high neutrophils, high protein, very low glucose; TB CSF: lymphocytes, very high protein, cobweb clot, raised ADA.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: T cells are effectors of adaptive (cell-mediated) immunity.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Macrophages phagocytose microbes and recognise them via pattern recognition receptors.

options.label: C
options.explanation: B cells produce antibodies in adaptive humoral immunity.

options.label: D
options.explanation: NK cells kill virus-infected and tumour cells without prior sensitisation.

questions.pearl: Innate immunity: neutrophils, macrophages, NK cells, dendritic cells, complement - rapid, non-specific, no memory.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Iron deficiency is the commonest cause of microcytic hypochromic anaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Reduced globin chain synthesis gives marked microcytosis, often with a normal or high RBC count.

options.label: C
options.explanation: B12 deficiency causes macrocytic megaloblastic anaemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lead inhibits haem synthesis, causing microcytic anaemia with basophilic stippling.

questions.pearl: Mentzer index (MCV/RBC) below 13 favours thalassaemia trait; above 13 favours iron deficiency.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Hepatitis viruses spread by the faeco-oral route:

options.label: A
options.explanation: HBV spreads parenterally, sexually and vertically.

options.label: B
options.explanation: HAV is transmitted faeco-orally through contaminated food and water.

options.label: C
options.explanation: HEV is waterborne faeco-oral; dangerous in pregnancy with high mortality.

options.label: D
options.explanation: HCV spreads mainly through blood (transfusion, IV drug use).

questions.pearl: Faeco-oral hepatitis: A and E (the vowels - they come from the bowels).

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Innocent murmurs are systolic (or continuous venous hum), never purely diastolic.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Still's murmur and pulmonary flow murmur are best heard at the left sternal edge.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Innocent murmurs are localised and do not radiate.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Heart sounds are normal in innocent murmurs; loud S1 suggests pathology such as mitral stenosis.

questions.pearl: Innocent murmur 'S's: Soft, Systolic, Short, Sounds normal, Symptomless, Standing/Sitting varies, Special tests normal.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Active management of third stage of labour (AMTSL):

options.label: A
options.text: Injection of oxytocin within 1 minute of delivery
options.explanation: Oxytocin 10 IU IM within 1 minute of the baby's birth is the key component.

options.label: B
options.text: Delivery of placenta by controlled cord traction
options.explanation: CCT with counter-traction on the uterus speeds placental delivery.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Manual removal is reserved for retained placenta, not a routine part of AMTSL.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fundal massage after placental delivery keeps the uterus contracted.

questions.pearl: AMTSL reduces PPH by about 60%; oxytocin is the uterotonic of choice.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Nephrotic syndrome is defined by proteinuria above 3.5 g/day.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Myeloma causes heavy proteinuria from Bence Jones light chains (and AL amyloid).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Renal amyloid deposition is a classic cause of nephrotic-range proteinuria.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acute nephritic glomerulonephritis usually gives modest proteinuria with haematuria, hypertension and oliguria.

questions.pearl: Urine dipstick does not detect Bence Jones protein; use urine electrophoresis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Drugs absorbed from the GIT by active transport:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Paracetamol is absorbed by passive diffusion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lipophilic diazepam crosses membranes by passive diffusion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Levodopa uses the large neutral amino acid carrier, so protein meals reduce its absorption.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ferrous iron is actively absorbed in the duodenum via DMT1.

questions.pearl: Most drugs are absorbed by passive diffusion; actively transported ones resemble nutrients (levodopa, iron, methyldopa, 5-FU).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Malnutrition is the commonest cause of secondary immunodeficiency worldwide.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Asplenia predisposes to overwhelming infection with encapsulated organisms.

options.label: C
options.explanation: HIV depletes CD4 T cells, causing acquired immunodeficiency.

options.label: D
options.explanation: X-linked conditions (e.g. Bruton agammaglobulinaemia) are primary, inherited immunodeficiencies.

questions.pearl: Post-splenectomy: vaccinate against pneumococcus, Hib and meningococcus, ideally 2 weeks before elective surgery.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ageing reduces collagen synthesis, angiogenesis and cell proliferation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Poorly vascularised adipose tissue and tension increase infection and dehiscence.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Stress raises cortisol, which impairs inflammation and collagen synthesis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Vitamin C is required for collagen hydroxylation and promotes healing; only its deficiency delays healing.

questions.pearl: Commonest local cause of delayed wound healing: infection; systemic: diabetes, steroids, malnutrition.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pregnancy is the commonest cause of secondary amenorrhoea; always exclude it first.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mullerian agenesis (MRKH) causes primary amenorrhoea.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Turner syndrome usually presents with primary amenorrhoea due to streak gonads.

options.label: D
options.explanation: PCOS causes oligomenorrhoea or secondary amenorrhoea from anovulation.

questions.pearl: Secondary amenorrhoea = no menses for 3 months (regular cycles) or 6 months (irregular) after previous menstruation.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Signs and symptoms of chronic kidney disease:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Reduced erythropoietin causes normocytic normochromic anaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: CKD usually causes hypertension from salt and water retention and renin activation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Uraemic pericarditis is an indication for urgent dialysis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Reduced phosphate excretion causes hyperphosphataemia.

questions.pearl: CKD-mineral bone disorder: high phosphate, low calcium, low calcitriol, secondary hyperparathyroidism.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Features of upper motor neuron lesion:

options.label: A
options.explanation: UMN lesions cause spasticity (hypertonia), except during the acute shock phase.

options.label: B
options.explanation: UMN lesions give an extensor plantar (Babinski) response.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Sustained clonus reflects loss of descending inhibition.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hyperreflexia is characteristic of UMN lesions.

questions.pearl: LMN lesion: wasting, fasciculation, hypotonia, hyporeflexia, flexor plantars.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rebound tenderness indicates localised peritonitis in the right iliac fossa.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Murphy's sign indicates acute cholecystitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Anorexia, nausea and vomiting follow the onset of pain.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pressure in the left iliac fossa causes pain in the right iliac fossa.

questions.pearl: Alvarado score (MANTRELS): Migration of pain, Anorexia, Nausea, Tenderness RIF, Rebound, Elevated temperature, Leucocytosis, Shift to left.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt decompresses the portal system for refractory bleeding or ascites.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Terlipressin causes splanchnic vasoconstriction, reducing portal pressure in variceal bleeding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Dietary sodium restriction is first-line for ascites.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Spironolactone with or without furosemide is used for ascites.

questions.pearl: Primary prophylaxis of variceal bleeding: non-selective beta blocker (propranolol, carvedilol) or band ligation.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Low plasma oncotic pressure causes transudation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Low albumin from any cause gives transudative effusion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Malignancy causes exudative effusions (often blood-stained).

options.label: D
options.explanation: CCF is the commonest cause of transudative effusion from raised hydrostatic pressure.

questions.pearl: Light's criteria (exudate): pleural/serum protein above 0.5, pleural/serum LDH above 0.6, or pleural LDH above two-thirds of the upper normal serum limit.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Viral and bacterial gastroenteritis are the commonest causes of infectious diarrhoea.

options.label: B
options.explanation: C. difficile causes antibiotic-associated diarrhoea and pseudomembranous colitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: IBD is an immune-mediated, non-infectious cause of diarrhoea.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Colorectal cancer causes altered bowel habit but is not infectious.

questions.pearl: C. difficile is treated with oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin; stop the offending antibiotic.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Breech is the commonest malpresentation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Vertex (cephalic) presentation is the normal presentation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Shoulder presentation occurs with transverse lie.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Brow presentation presents the largest diameter (mentovertical, 14 cm) and causes obstruction.

questions.pearl: Malpresentations: breech, face, brow, shoulder, compound; occipito-posterior is a malposition.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Shigella invades colonic mucosa causing bloody mucoid stools.

options.label: B
options.explanation: V. parahaemolyticus usually causes watery diarrhoea after seafood.

options.label: C
options.explanation: ETEC produces toxins causing watery traveller's diarrhoea.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Severe pseudomembranous colitis can produce bloody diarrhoea.

questions.pearl: Bloody diarrhoea organisms: Shigella, Campylobacter, Salmonella, EHEC (O157:H7), Entamoeba histolytica.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Common causes of maternal death in Bangladesh:

options.label: A
options.explanation: PPH is the leading cause of maternal death in Bangladesh.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Eclampsia/pre-eclampsia is the second leading cause.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Obstructed or prolonged labour contributes significantly to maternal deaths.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Twins increase risk but are not themselves a leading cause of death.

questions.pearl: Magnesium sulphate is the drug of choice to prevent and treat eclamptic seizures.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: High-risk HPV (16, 18) is found in over 99% of cervical cancers.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Early first pregnancy and high parity increase risk.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Early coitarche increases HPV exposure during cervical immaturity.

options.label: D
options.explanation: IUD use is not a risk factor; it may even be protective.

questions.pearl: Other risks: multiple partners, smoking, immunosuppression (HIV), long-term OCP use; VIA is used for screening in Bangladesh.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Generalised lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly are features of early congenital syphilis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Gummas of skin, palate and nasal septum occur in late congenital syphilis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Early congenital syphilis gives a copper-coloured maculopapular rash, often on palms and soles.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Argyll Robertson pupil is a feature of acquired tertiary neurosyphilis and is rare in congenital syphilis.

questions.pearl: Late congenital syphilis: Hutchinson triad - notched incisors, interstitial keratitis, eighth nerve deafness.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: ACE inhibitors are first-line antihypertensives, especially in young non-black patients and diabetics.

options.label: B
options.explanation: ACE inhibitors reduce mortality in HFrEF by lowering afterload and remodelling.

options.label: C
options.explanation: ACE inhibitors are teratogenic (fetal renal damage, oligohydramnios) and contraindicated in pregnancy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone and raise potassium; hyperkalaemia is a contraindication.

questions.pearl: ACE inhibitor dry cough is due to bradykinin accumulation; switch to an ARB.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Reduced renal excretion causes hyperkalaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Decreased phosphate excretion causes hyperphosphataemia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Dilutional hyponatraemia from water retention is common.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Low calcitriol and high phosphate cause hypocalcaemia.

questions.pearl: Hyperkalaemia above 6.5 mmol/L with ECG changes: IV calcium gluconate first to stabilise the myocardium.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: CK-MB rises in 4-6 h, peaks at 24 h and normalises in 2-3 days; useful for reinfarction.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Troponins are the most sensitive and specific markers, raised for 7-14 days.

options.label: C
options.explanation: LDH (LDH1 > LDH2 'flip') is a late marker peaking at 3-6 days; now largely obsolete but a recognised marker.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Myoglobin is the earliest marker (1-2 h) but non-specific.

questions.pearl: Earliest marker: myoglobin; most specific: troponin; best for reinfarction: CK-MB; late marker: LDH.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Referred otalgia may be due to:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Acute suppurative otitis media causes primary otalgia from the ear itself.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Peritonsillar abscess refers pain via the glossopharyngeal nerve (Jacobson's nerve).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Dental disease refers pain via the trigeminal nerve (auriculotemporal branch).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hypopharyngeal cancer refers pain via the vagus (Arnold's nerve).

questions.pearl: Referred otalgia nerves: V, VII, IX, X and C2-C3; unexplained otalgia in an adult smoker needs evaluation for hidden malignancy.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: It ventilates and drains the middle ear into the nasopharynx.

options.label: B
options.explanation: It enters the nasopharynx above the upper border of the superior constrictor (sinus of Morgagni) without piercing the fascia.

options.label: C
options.text: Gives attachment to the tensor veli palatini muscle
options.explanation: Tensor veli palatini arises partly from the tube and opens it during swallowing.

options.label: D
options.text: Can be obstructed by palatine tonsils
options.explanation: The tubal opening is obstructed by enlarged adenoids (nasopharyngeal tonsil), not palatine tonsils.

questions.pearl: The Eustachian tube is shorter, wider and more horizontal in children, predisposing to otitis media.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: About 80% arise from infected lower second and third molars.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Elevation of the tongue and floor-of-mouth swelling cause dysphagia and drooling.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Backward displacement of the tongue and laryngeal oedema can cause airway obstruction.

options.label: D
options.text: Incision and drainage is the treatment of choice
options.explanation: Airway protection and high-dose IV antibiotics are first-line; surgical decompression is for non-responders or abscess.

questions.pearl: Ludwig's angina is bilateral cellulitis of submandibular, sublingual and submental spaces; airway compromise is the main killer.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Aetiology of head and neck carcinoma:

options.label: A
options.explanation: HPV-16 is a major cause of oropharyngeal (tonsil, tongue base) squamous cell carcinoma.

options.label: B
options.explanation: UV exposure causes carcinoma of the lip (especially lower lip) and skin of the head and neck.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Previous radiation exposure to the neck increases the risk of thyroid and other head and neck cancers.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A diet rich in fruit and vegetables is protective; tobacco, alcohol and betel quid are the main risks.

questions.pearl: Epstein-Barr virus is linked to nasopharyngeal carcinoma; tobacco and alcohol act synergistically for other head and neck SCC.
